review.overview: PR #403 (feat: stage shared Railway queue, head 143990e) does two things in the evidence. It moves the scraper's BullMQ usage behind a new private workspace package, @package/queue. It also adds a second Railway Redis resource, pocket-trash-queue, to the IaC next to the existing scraper-queue, with RDB and AOF persistence in its start command. In code, the scraper builds its queues from env.REDIS_URL through a BullMQ adapter in packages/queue. The scraper IaC leaves REDIS_URL as preserve(), so no checked-in file binds the scraper service to either Redis resource. The preview deploy workflow still builds the preview REDIS_URL reference from scraper-queue. docs/railway.md describes pocket-trash-queue as the intended target after a separate, unapproved cutover. The Discord bot appears only in docs. No bot source is in the supplied evidence. One diagram follows. No schema or ER diagram is drawn because the PR has no schema changes in the evidence.

review.overview: PR #403 establishes a transport-independent queue boundary via the new @package/queue package. Applications define typed queues through this package, owning payload schemas, worker modes, retry/retention settings, and deduplication policies. The package encapsulates BullMQ and ioredis in production while exposing a portable contract. A deterministic in-memory adapter implements the same contract for tests. Railway infrastructure stages a new shared Redis resource (pocket-trash-queue) alongside the legacy scraper-queue during migration.

changedAreas.summary: New shared queue package at packages/queue/ containing transport-independent contract (index.ts), BullMQ production adapter (bullmq.ts), test utilities (test-contract.ts, contract.test.ts), and integration tests (bullmq.integration.test.ts). Exports portable types: QueueAdapter, DefinedQueue, QueueDefinition, QueueJob, QueueEnqueueResult, QueueProcessResult, QueueLifecycleEvent.

Scraper migrated from direct BullMQ usage to @package/queue. apps/scraper/src/queue/queues.ts now creates scraper queues via createScraperQueues() using transport adapter injection. Defines scraper-items and scraper-images queues with shared policy (5 retries, exponential backoff, 24h retention). Queue processor at apps/scraper/src/queue/processor.ts refactored to use portable QueueJob and DefinedQueue interfaces.

.railway/railway.ts modified to declare both legacyScraperQueue (retained) and sharedQueue (pocket-trash-queue) resources. Staged additive provisioning prevents cutover during IaC apply. Both use redis-volume (5GB). Shared queue includes AOF persistence (appendonly yes, appendfsync everysec). Migration procedure documented in docs/railway.md lines 104-134.

ScraperItemJob and ScraperImageJob discriminated union types in apps/scraper/src/scraper-types.ts define 11 job variants across 5 source types. Payloads validated via Zod schemas in apps/scraper/src/queue/queues.ts. Queue names scraper-items and scraper-images retained for compatibility.

.github/workflows/deploy.yml references RAILWAY_SCRAPER_QUEUE_PREVIEW_SERVICE_NAME as scraper-queue (line 30). Preview workflow sets REDIS_URL via Railway service reference ${{scraper-queue.REDIS_PUBLIC_URL}} (line 664). Workflow cutover to pocket-trash-queue pending approved migration stages.

review.overview: PR 403 (feat: stage shared Railway queue) adds a transport-independent queue package at packages/queue, migrates apps/scraper item and image queues onto its QueueAdapter contract, stages a shared Railway Redis resource named pocket-trash-queue in .railway/railway.ts while retaining the legacy scraper-queue resource, and documents a six-stage migration and cutover plan. The scraper keeps its existing stable queue names scraper-items and scraper-images (apps/scraper/src/scraper-types.ts:41-44). Production adapter transport (BullMQ over ioredis) is now owned by packages/queue rather than the scraper (packages/queue/src/bullmq.ts:23, decisions/architecture/eng-497-shared-queue-boundary.md:17-21). Declared IaC resources, documented cutover intent, and workflow-staged preview bindings are kept distinct below; no runtime Redis attachment for the production scraper service is verifiable from the supplied evidence.

changedAreas.summary: Defines the transport-independent DefinedQueue and QueueAdapter contract (packages/queue/src/index.ts:172-250), a BullMQ and ioredis production adapter owning one shared Redis connection per adapter (packages/queue/src/bullmq.ts:23-46), and a deterministic in-memory adapter for tests (packages/queue/src/index.ts:276-496). The decision record states the package owns BullMQ and ioredis in production and that scraper and bot code share queue policy without importing BullMQ (decisions/architecture/eng-497-shared-queue-boundary.md:17-32).

createScraperQueues now defines both bounded queues through the shared adapter with unchanged physical names scraper-items and scraper-images (apps/scraper/src/queue/queues.ts:297-324, name source apps/scraper/src/scraper-types.ts:41-44). createScraperJobContext opens the checkpoint Redis connection and the queues from the same env.REDIS_URL and verifies the checkpoint connection with ping before use (apps/scraper/src/jobs.ts:117-129). The processor drains items then images and supports redriveFailed dead-letter retries (apps/scraper/src/queue/processor.ts:297-445).

The IaC file stages a shared Redis resource pocket-trash-queue with appendonly yes and appendfsync everysec while retaining the legacy scraper-queue resource and the unchanged redis-volume (railway.ts as .railway/railway.ts:26-56). The scraper service declares REDIS_URL with preserve only (railway.ts:103), so this change declares resources without verifying or performing any runtime cutover, matching the documented staging intent (docs/railway.md:104-134).

The preview path continues to resolve REDIS_URL from the legacy scraper-queue service reference REDIS_PUBLIC_URL (deploy.yml:30, 664, 720-725) and redeploys that queue service from source before the native scraper deploy (deploy.yml:784-833). The workflow stages DATABASE_URL, Bunny image prefix, cron flag, and logging metadata on the preview scraper service with --skip-deploys (deploy.yml:692-746), consistent with the documented handoff that keeps scraper-queue until the approved cutover (docs/railway.md:261-276).

docs/railway.md records the shared Redis migration plan and cutover stages (docs/railway.md:104-134), the documented REDIS_URL service reference to pocket-trash-queue for the scraper and the Discord bot (docs/railway.md:205-212), and preview queue usage (docs/railway.md:261-276). docs/infrastructure-diagram.yaml adds a production pocket-trash-queue node with RDB and AOF and a scraper-to-queue edge labelled scraper-images and scraper-items (docs/infrastructure-diagram.yaml:74-77, 113-115). Changesets and the root railpack.json and .railwayignore support the staging (files 0, 1, 5, 34 of the PR).
